In         the          final        torque        expression
   𝜏= 𝑀(𝛩)𝛩̈ + 𝑉(𝛩, 𝛩̇ ) + 𝐺(𝛩)
      derived for the RP manipulator, what distinguishes the vector
     𝑉(𝛩, 𝛩̇) from 𝐺(𝛩)?

originalOptions.text:
𝑉(𝛩, 𝛩̇)depends only on  joint  position, while  𝐺(𝛩)
     depends only on joint velocity.

𝑉(𝛩, 𝛩̇ )  represents  centrifugal  and  Coriolis  terms
     depending on joint velocities, while 𝐺(𝛩) represents gravity
      terms depending only on joint position.

𝑉(𝛩, 𝛩̇ )and 𝐺(𝛩) are identical and represent the same
      physical effect.

𝑉(𝛩, 𝛩̇) is the mass matrix, while 𝐺(𝛩) is the damping
      matrix.

originalSourceText:
Q.7  In         the          final        torque        expression
   𝜏= 𝑀(𝛩)𝛩̈ + 𝑉(𝛩, 𝛩̇ ) + 𝐺(𝛩)
      derived for the RP manipulator, what distinguishes the vector
     𝑉(𝛩, 𝛩̇) from 𝐺(𝛩)?

     A) 𝑉(𝛩, 𝛩̇)depends only on  joint  position, while  𝐺(𝛩)
     depends only on joint velocity.

     B)  𝑉(𝛩, 𝛩̇ )  represents  centrifugal  and  Coriolis  terms
     depending on joint velocities, while 𝐺(𝛩) represents gravity
      terms depending only on joint position.

     C) 𝑉(𝛩, 𝛩̇ )and 𝐺(𝛩) are identical and represent the same
      physical effect.

     D) 𝑉(𝛩, 𝛩̇) is the mass matrix, while 𝐺(𝛩) is the damping
      matrix.

     Answer: B
      Refer to Lecture 14: Lagrangian Formulation of Manipulator
     Dynamics Slide 19
